title: Sequence
summary: An ordered family of values indexed by a specified set, usually the natural numbers.

context.note: Context is named textually in this seed release; its foundations are not yet recursively expanded into QEVA records.

assumptions.text: An index set I and codomain X are specified.

content.plain: A sequence is not merely a written list; mathematically it is a function whose input is an index.
content.exact: A sequence in X indexed by I is a function a:I→X. When I=N, the value at n is written a_n.
content.example: The sequence 1,2,4,8,... can be represented by a_n=2^n for n=0,1,2,...

relations.note: Recurrence relations constrain indexed values of sequences.
Sequence periodicity compares values at shifted indices.

verification.method: QEVA seed formulation checked editorially for mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA seed archive
provenance.source_note: Seed record written to demonstrate QEVA Protocol 0.1; it is not claimed to be the unique foundational presentation of this concept.
